s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss in one eye with optic disc swelling and retinal vascular occlusion in a patient undergoing immunotherapy
salient_findings: Sudden vision loss in the right eye
Marked swelling of the optic disc
Peripapillary retinal hemorrhages and occlusion of the superior branch artery
Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 40s
Presented with blurred vision in the right eye
Undergoing treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab, and bevacizumab
Initial visual acuity was 20/25 OU
Right eye had full visual field and relative afferent pupillary defect
Mild swelling of the optic disc on initial examination
Normal fundus and visual function in the left eye
MRI showed focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve
Lumbar puncture showed no abnormalities
Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm
Immunohistochemistry was positive for glial fibrillary acid protein and mutant IDH-1 protein

shortlist.label: Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm and immunohistochemistry was positive for glial fibrillary acid protein and mutant IDH-1 protein

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is undergoing immunotherapy and presented with sudden vision loss and optic disc swelling

shortlist.label: Metastatic Cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is undergoing treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab, and bevacizumab, which may increase the risk of metastatic disease

shortlist.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with sudden vision loss and combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein

shortlist.label: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with sudden vision loss and combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with blurred vision, relative afferent pupillary defect, and optic disc swelling, combined with the MRI findings of focal enhancement along the enlarged optic nerve and the vitreous biopsy showing an astrocytic neoplasm, suggests a diagnosis of Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma, especially given the patient's immunocompromised state due to treatment with durvalumab and bevacizumab.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Too broad, as lymphoma can occur in various parts of the body, and the specific location and context suggest a more specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Metastatic Cancer
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of a primary cancer, and the biopsy results suggest a primary CNS process.

rejected.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
rejected.why: While the patient did develop central retinal artery occlusion, it appears to be a secondary event following the primary process affecting the optic nerve and retina.

rejected.label: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion
rejected.why: Similar to central retinal artery occlusion, this seems to be a secondary complication rather than the primary diagnosis.
